teaser.en: A single breadfruit, roasted or simmered in coconut milk, can feed a family, and it grows on a tree.

summary.en: Breadfruit is a handsome tree with huge lobed leaves and round, starchy fruits, planted at the coast. The fruit is baked or boiled, often in coconut milk, and eaten like a vegetable.

about.en:
Breadfruit is a tall, spreading evergreen tree with very large, glossy leaves deeply cut into lobes, which make it easy to recognise even from a distance. Cut any part of it and a sticky white latex flows.

The fruits are round to oval, about the size of a large grapefruit, with a green skin patterned in small bumps or plates. Inside is pale, starchy flesh that becomes soft and bread-like when cooked.

where.en: Breadfruit is planted at the coast, usually near homes and in old town gardens, where a single tree can shade a whole yard.

uses.en: The fruit is eaten while still firm and starchy, before it turns sweet. It is baked or boiled, and often cooked in coconut milk, much like cassava or green bananas.

names.en: No Digo name has been recorded yet. Swahili: *mshelisheli*, with the fruit called *shelisheli*. English: breadfruit. Scientists call it *Artocarpus altilis*. It is a close relative of the jackfruit.

reason.en: Cassava, another starch cooked in coconut milk
Plantain, also cooked as a starchy vegetable
Coconut, whose milk cooks the fruit

sources: Maundu & Tengnäs (eds.) (2005) Useful Trees and Shrubs for Kenya, ICRAF/World Agroforestry species sheet https://apps.worldagroforestry.org/usefultrees/pdflib/Artocarpus_heterophyllus_KEN.pdf (remarks on A. altilis)
